scope: A bounded review of the finance and tax commitments on printed page 4 of ANO's final 2025 national election programme.

source.title: Program pro váš lepší život — program hnutí ANO do parlamentních voleb 2025
source.verification: The current official PDF was downloaded again, matched the previously retained copy byte-for-byte, and printed page 4 was visually checked. The visual check confirmed the retained source wording over conflicting search-index OCR variants.

earlierSourceReview.title: Lepší Česko — srpen/září 2025
earlierSourceReview.attributionBoundary: The relevant passages are Tier B statements by named ANO politicians inside an official national campaign publication. They are retained as earlier occurrences but are not used as the active first-version promise source.
earlierSourceReview.result: The earlier publication is consistent with the later programme on the working-student credit and the 2026 self-employed contribution increase. Its Digital Tax Cobra description uses a different detection scope, and one benefit occurrence addresses firms rather than employees. The final programme is later and remains the active wording for every admitted promise.

reviews.reason: The priority heading promises only to tackle the grey economy and lower taxes, without a concrete measure or target. The more specific commitments below are reviewed separately.

The detailed paragraph is split. This batch tracks the directly observable commitment not to adopt the euro; the broader promise to take no steps towards adoption needs a separate progress boundary before admission.

The passage combines growth, tax enforcement, administrative changes, asset management, annual operating-cost reductions, and a deficit outcome. Each potential commitment needs separate review without carrying the passage's causal claims into another promise.

Neither the promised reduction in tax evasion nor the increase in collection efficiency has a source-defined baseline or target, and the stated revenue effect cannot be fairly attributed without inventing a causal test.
The wording names tools but does not define how much the VAT gap must fall; the adjacent ambition to rank among Europe's leaders is also not a source-defined measurable threshold.
Introducing the named analytical system with the stated fraud-detection function can be verified from official administrative and implementation records.
The promised legislation, legal power, asset class, and cross-border money-laundering context are concrete and publicly verifiable.
The programme does not identify which Customs Administration powers would be expanded, so a fair completion boundary cannot be stated without adding scope.
This accepted original programme occurrence already produces the reviewed matching promise ano-2025-eet-2; this batch does not create another promise from it.
A general promise to lower taxes gradually has no tax, rate, amount, or deadline. The concrete tax changes in the following sentences are reviewed separately.

The composite sentence is split into independently assessable tax-credit commitments. The preschool credit was already reviewed; this batch adds only the working-student credit. The spouse-credit wording remains outside this batch because the exact reference point of 'original form' needs a separate baseline review.
The affected group, direction, and scheduled 2026 increase are explicit and can be checked against binding contribution rules.
The composite sentence is split into two independently assessable commitments. The corporate-tax rate promise was already reviewed; this batch adds removal of the leisure-benefit cap.
The affected supplies and the 12% VAT rate are explicit and can be checked against binding tax law.
